network: ctx.serve() responder behind the kernel's realm proxy; the tarball under test is the only @ai-ecoverse/wasm-tls-engine installed, so the proxy terminates curl's CONNECT tunnels with it (leaf key from the engine, chain from the kernel CA)
checklist: realm-proxy.mjs (kernel, the consumer path): curl https through the kernel's realm proxy with this engine, TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2 pinned: the handshake completes at that version with a 256-bit EC leaf for CN=cert.test from the SLICC realm CA; exact bodies; a 300000-byte download by sha256 and a 170824-byte upload hashed by the far end (more than the engine's 64 KiB out and 40 KiB in buffers); two requests on one tunnel; a CA that did not sign the leaf is rc 60 and -k accepts it

lib/engine-api.mjs (ci, Node's TLS client against the engine's own API, as slicc-kernel's tls-engine.ts drives it): the factory instantiates from wasmBinary with every export index.d.ts names; a getRandomValues that throws makes tls_leaf_new return 0 with PSA - Insufficient entropy, not a JS throw, and the same fresh instance then makes a leaf that serves a handshake (#551); a leaf is a fresh P-256 key whose SPKI is all that leaves; TLS 1.3 and 1.2 verified against a self-signed CA as the session's host, ALPN http/1.1, tls_version 0x0304/0x0303, leaf + CA chain; the whole chain goes out (a root-only client accepts a leaf from an intermediate the engine sends, and refuses it without); an IP-literal leaf without SNI; 1 MiB up and 1 MiB down intact on each version; several requests, then close_notify both ways; the client's end gives tls_read TLS_EOF; 300 leaves alive at once; 1500 leaf/session cycles without heap growth

refusals (engine-api.mjs): a certificate for another key, the CA's own certificate and garbage are refused by tls_leaf_add_cert, with tls_strerror naming the error (PK / X509, never UNKNOWN ERROR CODE); no session without a chain (TLS_BADARG); a ClientHello whose SNI names another host fails the handshake; a client without the CA, and an expired leaf, are refused by the client; plaintext instead of a ClientHello is an SSL error, not a hang; tls_feed takes no more than its 40 KiB room

lib/client-api.mjs (ci, 17 cases, Node's TLS server against the engine's client sessions, as slicc-kernel#922 will drive them over a socket): TLS 1.3 and 1.2 verified against a caller's trust store, ALPN agreed from a wire-format list (none offered = none), the server's chain read back by tls_peer_der, 1 MiB each way; refused (MBEDTLS_ERR_X509_CERT_VERIFY_FAILED / BAD_CERTIFICATE with the right BADCERT flag): a CA the store does not hold, a leaf for another host, an expired leaf, a clientAuth-only extendedKeyUsage; a TLS 1.1-only server fails the handshake; an IP literal sends no SNI and verifies only against an iPAddress SAN (a dNSName spelling the address is refused); TLS_CLIENT_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY finishes and still reports NOT_TRUSTED/CN_MISMATCH; no session without a store or a server name while verification is required, nor with unknown flags or a bad ALPN list; no resumption (a second connection to an untrusted server is refused); roots.der loads as a bundle (> 100 roots, each a valid certificate, slicc.tls.roots dated) alongside a caller root; no entropy fails closed (no store, no session, PSA - Insufficient entropy) and the instance recovers; a store freed while a session holds it stays alive; TLS 1.3: a keep-alive response fed in one piece behind the NewSessionTickets comes out of tls_read without more input, twice on one connection the server keeps open (#1032); an absolute name (dot.test.) verifies against a dot.test leaf and sends SNI dot.test (#1033)

lib/client-api.mjs, 4.2.0-4 (slicc-kernel#1004): tls_last_alert is 116 (certificate_required) from a TLS 1.3 Node server requiring a client certificate, on the read after the handshake, and 40 (handshake_failure) from a TLS 1.2 one, at the handshake; -1 before any alert, for a clean session and for a server session

lib/client-api.mjs, 4.2.0-3 (slicc-kernel#1004): tls_ciphersuite is the IANA number of the suite a Node server was pinned to, on TLS 1.3 and 1.2 (0 before the handshake); tls_client_cert: a Node server with requestCert and rejectUnauthorized accepts the client's chain and sees its CN, a client without one is refused, and the key and passphrase bytes the engine was given are zero afterwards; a PKCS#8 or SEC1 DER key and an AES-256-CBC encrypted PKCS#8 PEM with its passphrase load, a wrong passphrase (still wiped), a key for another certificate (TLS_BADARG, nothing kept), a non-DER chain, an empty chain or key, a second call and a call after the handshake started are refused; TLS_CLIENT_NO_SNI sends no servername and checks the name exactly as with SNI: a leaf for another host is refused, client.test. (trailing dot) verifies, and an IP literal verifies against an iPAddress SAN and is refused by a dNSName spelling it; TLS_CLIENT_VERIFY_CHAIN_ONLY connects to a trusted leaf for another host with tls_verify_result 0, tls_name_mismatch 1 and SNI sent, 0 for the right host, and still refuses an untrusted CA and an expired leaf; only flags 0, 1, 2, 4, 1|2 and 2|4 make a session: CHAIN_ONLY|INSECURE (with or without NO_SNI) and unknown bits are TLS_BADARG

lib/client-api.mjs, 4.2.0-5 (slicc-kernel#1090): tls_chain_verify checks a chain without a handshake as a client session would, through the session's own name routines; it returns 0 only when verified, 1 with the reasons when it verified and failed, < 0 for errors: a good chain plus host is 0/0 (an absolute name too, with or without the CA in the chain); a wrong host is 1/CN_MISMATCH and passes only with a NULL hostname; an empty hostname is CN_MISMATCH; an untrusted CA is NOT_TRUSTED, an expired leaf EXPIRED, a clientAuth-only leaf EXT_KEY_USAGE; an IP literal verifies against an iPAddress SAN and is CN_MISMATCH for a dNSName spelling it; a NULL store, no chain, a truncated DER, garbage and tls_test_chain_verify_alloc_error() are < 0 with flags 0xffffffff, and the next call verifies again; a NULL flags pointer is TLS_BADARG; 2000 verifications leave the heap size unchanged

4.2.0-6 (homescoop#1042): tls_client_new_name(ca, servername, servername_len, alpn, alpn_len, flags) takes the name by length and refuses a NUL byte inside it, an empty name with verification required and a name too long for the session (TLS_BADARG, no session); a plain name verifies and sends that SNI. tls_client_new stays the C-string form, documented as ending the name at its first NUL (cert/lib/client-api.mjs). 4.2.0-5 has no tls_client_new_name (NEGATIVE.md)

4.2.0-6 (homescoop#1091): tls_strerror names TLS_EOF, TLS_NOMEM and TLS_BADARG as 'tls-engine - …', not the Mbed TLS HMAC_DRBG codes with the same values; the text of tls_last_error() after a refused tls_client_new has no HMAC_DRBG or UNKNOWN ERROR CODE. 4.2.0-5: 'HMAC_DRBG - Too many random requested in single call'

4.2.0-6 (homescoop#1121): tls_client_cert accepts an RSA-2048 client key as PKCS#8 DER, PKCS#8 PEM, encrypted PKCS#8 PEM (passphrase) and PKCS#1 PEM/DER, the key bytes wiped, and a Node server with requestCert/rejectUnauthorized sees the PKCS#8 one's certificate; an RSA key for another certificate (PKCS#8 and PKCS#1) is still refused at tls_client_cert with TLS_BADARG, before any handshake (zzy4's condition: the kernel maps it to ERR_OSSL_X509_KEY_VALUES_MISMATCH). 4.2.0-5 refuses every PKCS#8 RSA key

4.2.0-7 (homescoop#1376): tls_client_cert accepts RSA-4096 and RSA-8192 client keys (PKCS#1 DER and PKCS#8 PEM, the key bytes wiped), a Node server with requestCert/rejectUnauthorized sees each one's certificate after a handshake, and a key for another certificate of the same size is TLS_BADARG; a leaf with an 8200-bit RSA key, alone or with its CA, is refused with TLS_RSA_TOO_LARGE (-0x10000), which tls_strerror names 'tls-engine - RSA key larger than 8192 bits (TLS_RSA_TOO_LARGE)'. 4.2.0-6 refuses RSA-8192 with -15104 PK - The pubkey tag or value is invalid (NEGATIVE.md)

4.2.0-8 (homescoop#1638, slicc-kernel#1401), lib/server-api.mjs (ci, Node's tls.connect against the engine's new server sessions): tls_leaf_import makes a leaf from the caller's chain and key, parsed and matched as tls_client_cert does: self-signed RSA-2048 and P-256 leaves each serve Node with ca set to that certificate over TLS 1.3 and 1.2, and a P-384 leaf and an intermediate's leaf (the chain sent whole to a root-only client) serve too; RSA PKCS#8 DER/PEM, PKCS#1 PEM/DER, SEC1 PEM/DER and encrypted PKCS#8 PEM with the passphrase load, the key and passphrase bytes wiped; a wrong or missing passphrase is Mbed TLS's PK error, a key for another certificate (RSA, EC, and RSA for an EC leaf) TLS_BADARG, an 8200-bit RSA leaf TLS_RSA_TOO_LARGE, an empty chain or key TLS_BADARG, and no tls_strerror text holds the passphrase or a 16-character run of the key's PEM or DER hex; one imported leaf serves two sessions after tls_leaf_free, and 300 import/session cycles leave the heap unchanged. tls_server_new: with ALPN [h2, http/1.1], a client offering http/1.1 agrees http/1.1, h2 or both (either order) agrees h2 (the server's preference), none agrees none, on both versions, and tls_alpn matches the client's view; a client offering only spdy/3 fails the handshake with NO_APPLICATION_PROTOCOL, and a server with no list agrees none; malformed ALPN lists are TLS_BADARG. tls_sni gives the client's servername (no requirement on it, case kept) and 0 when the client sends none or before the handshake, TLS_BADARG for a short buffer. REQUIRE_CERT (1.3 and 1.2) passes a client_ca certificate (tls_verify_result 0, tls_peer_der its DER) and fails the handshake without one, with one from another CA and with a serverAuth-only one; REQUEST_CERT passes without one (no peer), with a good one (verified), and with an untrusted one (tls_verify_result NOT_TRUSTED); flags 0 asks for nothing; flags 3, 4, -1, and either flag without client_ca are TLS_BADARG, as are a leaf without a chain and no leaf; tls_client_cert on a server session is TLS_BADARG. Regression: tls_session_new still agrees http/1.1 only, refuses another host's SNI, and tls_sni gives its host; engine-api.mjs 19/19 and client-api.mjs 33/33 unchanged. 4.2.0-7 has no tls_leaf_import (NEGATIVE.md)

4.2.0-9 (homescoop#1765, slicc-kernel#1499), lib/server-api.mjs: a tls_server_new session refusing a client sends an alert the client reads. REQUIRE_CERT over TLS 1.3: no certificate is alert 116 (certificate_required), a certificate from another CA 48 (unknown_ca), a serverAuth-only one 43 (unsupported_certificate), each read by openssl s_client (never 'bad record mac') and by Node's tls.connect; over TLS 1.2: no certificate is 40 (handshake_failure), the others 48 and 43; an ALPN mismatch is 120 to s_client on both versions; the engine's own client reads tls_last_alert 116 on the read after a TLS 1.3 handshake without a certificate, 48 with a certificate from another CA, 120 at the handshake for an ALPN mismatch, and -1 from a REQUEST_CERT server. server-refusal-alerts.patch: the TLS 1.3 server sends under its application keys from its Finished on, a missing certificate is 116 not 41, and TLS 1.2 sends 40 for one. The published 4.2.0-8 gives bad record mac on 1.3 and no alert on 1.2 (NEGATIVE.md)

4.2.0-9 (homescoop#1766, slicc-kernel#1501/#1502), lib/server-api.mjs: TLS_SERVER_SELECT (4) pauses a server session after the ClientHello: tls_handshake returns 2, tls_read/tls_write TLS_SELECT_PENDING (-4), nothing is sent; tls_sni and tls_client_alpn give the client's SNI and ALPN offer (wire format, client order), also after the handshake; tls_server_select sets the leaf (0 keeps tls_server_new's) and one ALPN protocol or none, and Node and openssl s_client (TLS 1.3 and 1.2) verify the selected leaf and agree the selected ALPN; a protocol the client didn't offer, a prefix or extension of one, no leaf, a leaf without a chain, a call before the ClientHello or after the selection are TLS_BADARG and leave it paused; tls_server_refuse sends 112, 120 or 40 (Node and s_client read it) and refuses other alerts; SELECT with an ALPN list or without SELECT and no leaf is TLS_BADARG, SELECT|REQUIRE_CERT requires the certificate (116 without one); the ClientHello fed byte by byte or split across two records pauses once whole; an alert record, plaintext, a ServerHello, an empty record (10), SSL 2 framing (70), a record over 16384 bytes (22), a 33-byte session id, an empty or overlong ALPN name, an empty SNI (50), two SNI or two ALPN extensions (47) and a 300-byte SNI (112) are refused with that alert and nothing kept; a TLS 1.3 HelloRetryRequest (brainpoolP256r1tls13 key share) pauses once and finishes with the selected leaf and ALPN; a selected leaf outlives tls_leaf_free, and 300 select cycles leave the heap unchanged. The published 4.2.0-8 has no tls_server_select (NEGATIVE.md)

4.2.0-10 (homescoop#1774, slicc-kernel#1504), lib/keylog.mjs (ci): TLS_KEYLOG (8) on tls_client_new/tls_client_new_name/tls_server_new sessions collects NSS key log lines that tls_keylog drains, each ending in \n: a server session's lines over TLS 1.3 (CLIENT_HANDSHAKE_TRAFFIC_SECRET, SERVER_HANDSHAKE_TRAFFIC_SECRET, CLIENT_TRAFFIC_SECRET_0, SERVER_TRAFFIC_SECRET_0) and TLS 1.2 (CLIENT_RANDOM) equal openssl s_client -keylogfile's and Node tls.connect's keylog lines for the same session, a client session's equal a Node server's, a SELECT|KEYLOG server's (s_client, 1.3) and a REQUEST_CERT|KEYLOG server's (Node, 1.2) too, and an engine client and server with the flag log the same lines; without the flag (client, server, SELECT, tls_session_new) no export callback is registered, the buffer stays zero, tls_keylog is 0, and no secret's hex (from Node's keylog of the same session) is anywhere in the wasm heap after a handshake on either version; tls_keylog hands out whole lines only (TLS_BADARG with nothing drained when max holds none), the buffer is zero after a drain, and once one side is drained and the other freed no secret's hex is left in the heap; with the bound lowered to 200 bytes only the first whole line is kept; TLS_KEYLOG combines with every allowed client and server flag and 16, KEYLOG|16, KEYLOG|INSECURE|CHAIN_ONLY, KEYLOG|REQUEST_CERT without client_ca and KEYLOG|3 stay TLS_BADARG. The published 4.2.0-9 has no tls_keylog and refuses flag 8 (NEGATIVE.md)

4.2.0-11 (homescoop#1799, slicc-kernel#1545), lib/keylog.mjs (ci): a TLS_KEYLOG session over TLS 1.3 logs five lines, EXPORTER_SECRET <client random> <exporter master secret> after the four traffic secrets, on client and server sessions, and every line equals one of the peer's, which also logs five: openssl s_client -keylogfile against a server session (plain and SELECT), Node tls.connect against a server session and a Node server against a client session, each pinned to TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (64 hex digits) and TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 (96; tls_ciphersuite 0x1301 and 0x1302); an engine client and server log the same EXPORTER_SECRET line, and it is drained and wiped like the others; TLS 1.2 is still one CLIENT_RANDOM line (no EXPORTER_SECRET from Node either), and without the flag nothing is armed or kept. The bound case and the 5-line drain case run with the new line. The published 4.2.0-10 has no EXPORTER_SECRET line: 14 of 19 keylog cases fail (NEGATIVE.md)

4.2.0-11, homescoop#1041 (coverage, lib/client-api.mjs): tls_client_new_name makes a session for a 255-byte name and refuses 256 bytes and a NULL name with a length (TLS_BADARG); tls_chain_verify verifies leaf plus intermediate (0/0) under a pathLen 1 root, flags the leaf alone NOT_TRUSTED and doesn't verify the reverse order, flags a not-yet-valid leaf FUTURE, fails closed (< 0, flags 0xffffffff) on trailing bytes after the last certificate and on a 256-byte hostname, and checks a 255-byte one (CN_MISMATCH). These pass on 4.2.0-10 too (gaps, not fixes)
